function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

Below is a **step‑by‑step playbook** you can follow to turn your e‑commerce idea into a polished, production‑ready front‑end. I’ll cover the whole stack – from design to deployment – and give you concrete code snippets, folder layouts, and tool recommendations. Feel free to skip sections that already fit your workflow. --- ## 1️⃣ Define the Scope & Gather Requirements | What | Why | Deliverable | |------|-----|-------------| | **Core pages** | Home, product list, product detail, cart, checkout, account, admin | Wireframes / Figma file | | **Features** | Search, filters, sorting, pagination, wishlist, reviews, live chat | Feature list | | **Performance goals** | < 200 ms first paint, < 1 kB bundle | KPI sheet | | **Accessibility** | WCAG 2.1 AA | Accessibility checklist | | **SEO** | Product pages indexable | SEO audit | > **Tip:** Use a shared design system (Figma + Storybook) so designers and devs stay in sync. --- ## 2️⃣ Pick a Front‑End Framework | Option | Pros | Cons | When to use | |--------|------|------|--------------| | **React + Next.js** | SSR/SSG, ISR, file‑based routing, rich ecosystem | Slight learning curve | Most e‑commerce sites | | **Vue + Nuxt.js** | Similar to Next, Vue‑centric | Smaller community | Vue‑only teams | | **SvelteKit** | Tiny bundle, reactive, SSR | Newer, fewer plugins | Performance‑critical projects | | **Angular** | Opinionated, built‑in services | Heavyweight | Enterprise teams | > **Recommendation:** Next.js (React) – it gives you SEO out of the box and a mature ecosystem for e‑commerce (e.g., `next-auth`, `stripe`, `react‑query`). --- ## 3️⃣ Set Up the Project Skeleton ```bash npx create-next-app@latest my-ecom --typescript cd my-ecom ``` ### Suggested folder layout ``` /components # Reusable UI components /pages # Routes (Next.js) /api # Serverless API routes (optional) /products # Product pages /cart /checkout /account /admin /lib # Utilities, hooks, services /styles # Global CSS / Tailwind config /public # Static assets /tests # Jest / Cypress ``` --- ## 4️⃣ Styling & Design System | Tool | Why | Quick start | |------|-----|-------------| | **Tailwind CSS** | Utility‑first, responsive, low CSS bloat | `npm i -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer && npx tailwindcss init -p` | | **Chakra UI** | Accessible components, themeable | `npm i @chakra-ui/react @emotion/react @emotion/styled framer-motion` | | **Material‑UI** | Rich component set | `npm i @mui/material @emotion/react @emotion/styled` | > **Tip:** Combine Tailwind for layout + Chakra for components. > Example: > ```tsx > > > > ``` --- ## 5️⃣ State Management | Option | When to use | |--------|-------------| | **React Context + useReducer** | Small to medium apps | | **Redux Toolkit** | Complex global state, many reducers | | **React Query** | Server‑state (products, cart, checkout) | | **Zustand** | Lightweight, no boilerplate | > **Typical pattern:** > *Product list* → fetch via `react-query` → store in local component state. > *Cart* → global context or Redux. > *Checkout* → form state + `react-hook-form`. --- ## 6️⃣ API Integration Assume you have a REST or GraphQL backend. If you’re using Next.js API routes, you can proxy calls: ```ts // pages/api/products/[id].ts import type { NextApiRequest, NextApiResponse } from 'next'; import axios from 'axios'; export default async function handler(req: NextApiRequest, res: NextApiResponse) { const { id } = req.query; const { data } = await axios.get(`https://api.example.com/products/${id}`); res.status(200).json(data); } ``` On the client: ```tsx // hooks/useProduct.ts import { useQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query'; import axios from 'axios'; export const useProduct = (id: string) => useQuery(['product', id], () => axios.get(`/api/products/${id}`).then(r => r.data)); ``` --- ## 7️⃣ Authentication & Authorization | Library | Notes | |---------|-------| | **next-auth** | OAuth, email, credentials, JWT | | **Auth0** | SaaS, social logins | | **Firebase Auth** | Real‑time, easy mobile sync | Example with `next-auth`: ```ts // pages/api/auth/[...nextauth].ts import NextAuth from 'next-auth'; import CredentialsProvider from 'next-auth/providers/credentials'; export default NextAuth({ providers: [ CredentialsProvider({ name: 'Credentials', credentials: { email: {}, password: {} }, async authorize(credentials) { const user = await db.findUserByEmail(credentials.email); if (user && user.password === credentials.password) return user; return null; }, }), ], callbacks: { async session({ session, token }) { session.user.id = token.sub; return session; }, }, }); ``` Use `useSession()` in components to guard routes. --- ## 8️⃣ Shopping Cart & Checkout Flow 1. **Cart Context** – holds items, quantities, total. 2. **Persist cart** – localStorage + sync with server on login. 3. **Checkout page** – collect shipping, billing, payment. 4. **Payment** – Stripe Elements or PayPal SDK. ```tsx // components/CheckoutForm.tsx import { CardElement, useStripe, useElements } from '@stripe/react-stripe-js'; export default function CheckoutForm() { const stripe = useStripe(); const elements = useElements(); const handleSubmit = async (e: React.FormEvent) => { e.preventDefault(); const { error, paymentMethod } = await stripe.createPaymentMethod({ type: 'card', card: elements.getElement(CardElement), }); if (!error) { // Send paymentMethod.id to your backend } }; return (
); } ``` --- ## 9️⃣ Performance Optimizations | Technique | How | |-----------|-----| | **Image optimization** | `` (Next.js) | | **Code splitting** | Dynamic imports (`next/dynamic`) | | **Lazy load** | `React.lazy` + `Suspense` | | **Prefetch** | `next/link` with `prefetch` | | **SSR/SSG** | `getStaticProps`, `getServerSideProps` | | **Cache headers** | `Cache-Control` in API routes | | **Bundle analysis** | `next-bundle-analyzer` | --- ## 🔟 Testing Strategy | Layer | Tool | Example | |-------|------|---------| | Unit | Jest + React Testing Library | `render( ); } ``` --- ## 1️⃣5️⃣ Final Checklist Before Launch - [ ] All core pages responsive (mobile, tablet, desktop) - [ ] Cart persists across sessions - [ ] Checkout works with test payments - [ ] SEO meta tags & structured data - [ ] Accessibility audit (axe, Lighthouse) - [ ] Performance audit (Lighthouse > 90) - [ ] Unit + E2E tests passing - [ ] CI pipeline builds & deploys - [ ] Analytics (GA4, Hotjar) integrated - [ ] Error monitoring (Sentry) --- ### 🎉 You’re ready! Pick the pieces that fit your team, iterate quickly, and keep the user experience at the center. Happy coding!
